newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria approves Japanese loan for power plant.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria approves Japanese loan for power plant.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Tuesday approved plans to fund the construction of a new coal-fired power plant with a Japanese government credit, a government spokeswoman said.

Bulgaria's Energy Ministry is negotiating the credit for the construction of a new 920-megawatt coal-fired plant in the country's biggest mining and power complex Maritsa East One. The plant is expected to cost some $605 million.

Experts from the Japanese Cooperation Agency (JICA) were helping Bulgaria work out a pilot project using electronic technology to reduce pollution from the high-sulphur lignite coal. Cabinet approval is a condition of the credit.
JICA would give the installation, worth $4 million, free to the Bulgarian energy ministry, an energy official said.
Environmental officials say lignite from Maritsa East has one of the highest sulphur contents in Europe and Bulgaria's outdated thermal power stations are among the worst polluters in the country.
Maritsa East, 250 km south-east of Sofia, has only lignite coal and its reserves of some two billion tonnes are expected to feed the country's coal-fired power stations for another 80 to 100 years.
Bulgaria relies on Maritsa East for 30 percent of its electricity needs and the nuclear power plant at Kozloduy meets more than 40 percent of the country's power demand.
